AI@HHMI:

The project aims to develop AI methods for mesoscale structural biology, understanding how cellular macromolecules organize into higher-order structures. You will work in a team at Janelia, with experimental and computational collaborators across the Rosen lab (UT Southwestern Medical Center/HHMI), Gouaux lab (Oregon Health and Science University/HHMI), Collepardo-Guevara lab (University of Cambridge), and Villa lab (UC San Diego/HHMI).

AutoStore is transforming how we operate, serve customers and partners, and scale our commercial organization.

Your first proving ground will be Sales Support, a global operation with rich data, complex workflows and significant opportunities for AI and automation. From there, the capabilities you build will expand across the broader Commercial organization.

business problem → prototype → production → measurable impact.

You will design AI-powered capabilities combining agentic AI, automation, enterprise data and workflow orchestration, including:
AI agents that understand requests, retrieve knowledge, reason across business rules and recommend or take actions
Intelligent case intake, classification, routing and prioritization
Automated order and PO quality validation
Knowledge and support agents grounded in enterprise data and documentation
AI-assisted exception handling and next-best actions
Pattern recognition across operational data to identify recurring issues and opportunities
Intelligent self-service experiences for employees, partners and customers

Build Agentic AI — Design, prototype and productionize AI agents and intelligent workflows using LLMs, RAG, tool use, orchestration and human-in-the-loop patterns.

Engineer for Production — Move beyond demos. Build secure, scalable and observable solutions with strong practices around APIs, integrations, testing, evaluation, monitoring and governance.
Deliver Measurable Impact — Measure success through outcomes such as cycle time, quality, manual touches, self-service, adoption and capacity created.
Scale Across Commercial — Take successful capabilities beyond Sales Support into sales productivity, partner and customer experience, revenue and account intelligence, and digital commercial experiences such as AutoStore Sphere.

We care more about what you can build and how you think than matching every technology on a checklist.
Strong software engineering skills, particularly Python and modern APIs
Experience building applications using LLMs, generative AI or agentic AI
Experience with RAG, enterprise search, tool/function calling or agent orchestration
Strong understanding of data, workflow automation and systems integration
Experience taking AI solutions from prototype to production
Understanding of AI evaluation, observability, security and responsible AI
Ability to turn ambiguous business problems into simple, scalable solutions
Curiosity, ownership and a strong bias toward action
Experience with Azure, Databricks, Salesforce, SAP, GitHub or modern AI development frameworks is valuable, but the ability to learn, connect systems and ship matters more than any specific technology.

AutoStore believes in taking care of employees and is dedicated to providing a supportive and rewarding work environment. Join us in our mission to store and move things for everyone, everywhere.

Health Savings Account (HSA) with a company contribution

Educational assistance and professional development programs, including mentorship/coaching programs with external industry leaders

Support and build assigned integration and application work across HR platforms including HCM, Benefits, Payroll, Recruiting, Identity Management, and vendor management systems, ensuring adherence to organizational patterns and standards.

Highly skilled in building with REST/SOAP and GraphQL, and proficient in data transformation patterns (XML, XSLT, JSON).
Demonstrated ownership of integration architecture, including event-driven patterns, API gateway patterns, and fault-tolerant design.
Deep understanding of the Workday data model and security fundamentals (domains, segments, business processes).
Bachelor’s degree from a recognized university in Engineering, Computer Science, IT, or a related field (B.E./B.Tech/MCA), or equivalent practical experience.
Nice-to-Have Qualifications
Experience with an iPaaS platform such as MuleSoft or Workato.
Workday Integration or Extend certification.

Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.
The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.
About The Role
We’re looking for an avionics engineer who is equally comfortable with a multimeter and a CAD model. You’ll own the electrical and electronic systems that make the aircraft fly: sensors, flight computers, radios, power, and the harnesses that tie it all together. You’ll work day to day with our embedded software team, but your focus is the hardware: integrating it, testing it, breaking it on the bench, and getting it ready for the aircraft.
This role is a fit for someone early in their career who has crossed the line between mechanical and electrical engineering, whether that’s an ME who kept ending up in the wiring or an EE who kept ending up in the airframe. If you’ve built and flown something, you’ll feel at home here.
What You’ll Do
Design, integrate, and test avionics subsystems including flight computers, GPS/INS, air data, datalinks, radios, and payload interfaces
Develop wiring harness designs, connector pinouts, and power distribution architecture, and get them built and installed
Build and run bench test setups and hardware-in-the-loop rigs alongside the embedded software team
Support ground testing, integration testing, and flight test campaigns, from preflight checkouts to post-flight data review
Troubleshoot hardware issues across electrical, mechanical, and software boundaries
Package avionics into the airframe with attention to weight, thermal, vibration, and maintainability
Help define and execute qualification testing for environmental, power quality, and EMI/EMC requirements
Write the documentation that lets the next person build, test, and fix it
What You’ll Bring
BS in Mechanical, Electrical, Aerospace, or Computer Engineering
1 to 4 years of hands-on experience with aircraft, UAVs, or comparable hardware systems (including significant student project or competition work)

Project Description
Hiredbuddy is seeking an entry-level Full Stack Developer to join our remote team. You'll build and maintain web applications, collaborate with cross-functional teams, and grow your skills in a supportive environment. If you're passionate about coding and ready to make an impact, apply today!
Full Description
As an Entry Level Full Stack Developer at Hiredbuddy, you will be an integral part of our engineering team, contributing to the design, development, and maintenance of web applications that serve a diverse client base. This remote role is perfect for someone who is eager to apply foundational coding skills in a real-world environment while learning from experienced professionals. You will work on both front-end and back-end components, ensuring seamless user experiences and robust server-side logic.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and maintain responsive web applications using modern JavaScript frameworks such as React or Vue.js for the front end.
Build and integrate RESTful APIs and microservices using Node.js, Express, or similar back-end technologies.
Write clean, maintainable, and well-documented code that follows industry best practices.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including designers, product managers, and other developers to deliver high-quality features.
Participate in code reviews, provide constructive feedback, and continuously improve development processes.
Troubleshoot and debug applications to optimize performance and ensure reliability.
Work with databases (SQL or NoSQL) to design schemas, write queries, and manage data storage.
Use version control systems like Git for collaborative development and deployment.
Stay updated with emerging technologies and suggest improvements to existing systems.
Assist in testing and deployment using CI/CD pipelines and cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure, or Heroku).
Technologies and Tools
Our stack evolves, but currently we rely on:
Front-end: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6+), React, Redux, or Vue.js
Back-end: Node.js, Express, Python (Django/Flask) or Ruby on Rails
Databases: PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or MySQL
Version Control: Git, GitHub/GitLab
Deployment: Docker, AWS, Netlify, Vercel
Testing: Jest, Mocha, Chai, Cypress
Communication: Slack, Zoom, Jira, Trello
Growth and Development
At Hiredbuddy, we invest in our team's growth. You will receive direct mentorship from senior engineers, regular feedback, and access to resources that help you advance your skills. We encourage exploration of new tools and technologies, and we provide a clear path for progression to mid-level and senior roles. Your contributions will directly impact the success of our products and the satisfaction of our clients.
Work Environment
This is a fully remote position, allowing you to work from anywhere within the United States. We value work-life balance and flexibility, while maintaining a strong sense of community through virtual events, pair programming sessions, and open communication channels. You will have the support you need to succeed, whether it's through structured onboarding, regular check-ins, or a dedicated buddy system.
If you are ready to launch your career as a Full Stack Developer and make a meaningful impact, we would love to hear from you.
Requirements
0-2 years of experience in full stack development (internships and personal projects count)
Proficiency in at least one front-end framework (React, Vue, or Angular) and one back-end language (Node.js, Python, or Ruby)
Understanding of RESTful APIs and HTTP fundamentals
Familiarity with relational and/or NoSQL databases
Knowledge of version control systems (Git)
Ability to write clean, testable code
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail
Excellent communication and teamwork abilities
Self-motivated and able to work independently in a remote environment
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
Benefits
Competitive entry-level salary with performance reviews
100% remote work flexibility
Health, dental, and vision insurance
Paid time off and public holidays
Home office stipend
Access to learning platforms and certification courses
Mentorship from senior developers
Opportunity for career growth and role advancement

About the Company
Capital OneJob Title: Associate Data Engineer (Entry-Level / Campus & Emerging Talent)Location: Remote (Eligible across the United States)Employment Type: Full-TimeCompany Overview Capital One is a technology-driven financial institution operating fully in the public cloud. We treat data as a primary product to power real-time fraud detection, personalized banking experiences, and predictive credit decisioning.
About the Role
As an Associate Data Engineer, you will join an engineering team dedicated to building resilient, high-throughput data platforms, modern pipelines, and data mesh architectures using cloud-native tools. In this entry-level role, you will design, develop, and maintain automated batch and streaming data pipelines. You will collaborate directly with software engineers, machine learning scientists, and product managers to ingest raw data, transform complex datasets, and deliver reliable data products to production data lakes and warehouses.
Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities
Data Pipeline Development: Write clean, modular, and maintainable code in Python, Scala, or Java to build ETL/ELT data pipelines.
Cloud Architecture: Build, configure, and monitor data processing workloads using AWS native services (S3, EMR, Glue, Lambda, and Kinesis).
Data Modeling & Storage: Support relational, document, and columnar data warehousing solutions (PostgreSQL, Snowflake, and Redshift) with efficient schemas, partitioning, and indexing.
Data Quality & Governance: Implement automated data validation checks, monitoring, schema drift detection, and data lineage tracking to maintain high data reliability in a regulated financial environment.
DevOps & Automation: Adopt CI/CD practices (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Terraform) to deploy data infrastructure as code and schedule jobs via orchestrators like Apache Airflow.
Agile Collaboration: Participate in sprint ceremonies, peer code reviews, backlog grooming, and technical problem-solving sessions.
Qualifications
Basic Qualifications
Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative STEM discipline (or equivalent practical technical training/bootcamp completion).
Programming: Academic, project, or internship experience coding in Python, SQL, Scala, or Java.
Database Fundamentals: Strong foundation in relational database management systems (RDBMS) and writing optimized SQL queries (joins, aggregations, window functions).
Work Authorization: Must possess valid, unrestricted U.S. work authorization. Capital One will sponsor a new applicant for employment authorization for this entry-level position (e.g., H-1B transfer or initial petition). Candidates holding permanent authorization (U.S. Citizen, Permanent Resident, Asylee/Refugee/OPT) or eligible status with current authorization to work for any employer are welcome to apply.
Required Skills
Academic, project, or internship experience coding in Python, SQL, Scala, or Java.
Strong foundation in relational database management systems (RDBMS) and writing optimized SQL queries (joins, aggregations, window functions).
Preferred Skills
Prior internship, capstone project, or open-source contribution in data engineering or cloud software development.
Familiarity with distributed computing engines such as Apache Spark or distributed messaging queues such as Apache Kafka.
Hands-on exposure to cloud environments, especially Amazon Web Services (AWS).
Knowledge of workflow orchestration tools like Apache Airflow.
Understanding of basic Git/GitHub version control workflows and automated testing practices.
Pay range and compensation package
Estimated Compensation & Benefits
Base Salary Range: $95,000 – $125,000 / year (commensurate with geographic location, education, and relevant experience).
Incentive Compensation: Discretionary year-end performance bonus and eligibility for 401(k) matching up to 7.5%.
Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance; remote home office setup stipend; flexible paid time off (PTO); parental leave; and tuition assistance/learning stipends.
Equal Opportunity Statement
Capital One is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity and inclusivity in the workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

About Pelico
Traditional industrial manufacturing systems were built for predictability. Supply chains no longer are. Today, real-time data is buried in legacy tools that weren't designed for constant disruption. By the time an issue surfaces, it has already snowballed, sending everyone into firefighting mode. Pelico exists to close the gap between production plans and the daily reality on the factory floor.
We've built the manufacturing orchestration platform trusted by the world's most complex industrial operations : companies like Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Eaton, and Cartier. Our AI connects fragmented supply chain, production, and quality data into a single live operational picture — then puts AI agents to work anticipating disruptions, simulating recovery options, and keeping every team aligned before small problems become expensive ones.
Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, 83North, and Serena, we've raised $72M and are growing fast — 300% year-over-year revenue growth, deployed in 15+ countries, and supporting factories worldwide. We're headquartered in Paris, with offices in Miami, London and Amsterdam, and we're just getting started.
This is a rare chance to join a company that's redefining an industry that hasn't been disrupted in decades — from the inside.
About The Role
Companies have multiple founding moments and Pelico is going through a new one.
You would be one of the founding engineers of our new agentic platform, building alongside a small, super talented, high-bar team. This is a hands-on seat from day one: you write the code that manufacturers and their own AI teams build on, close to real customers and real factory data.
You benefit from company assets (data, events dependency graphs, simulation engine, next best action algorithms) and the reach that comes from Pelico running the operational data of multiple leading manufacturers.
What You'll Do
Ship agent capabilities end to end. Build real features from the tool/MCP and orchestration backend through to the React console, live for users - not demos.
Harden the runtime. Durable execution, retries, scheduling, and human-in-the-loop approvals on agent actions that carry real consequences.
Make agents trustworthy. Grow the eval harness (scenario evals, LLM-as-judge) so we catch regressions in agent behavior before they ship.
Build a console people believe. Real-time streaming of agent events, tool calls, and approvals - clear, fast, and reliable enough that a controller trusts it.
Set a craft bar. Write specs others build against, keep the frontend/backend contract honest, and leave reusable patterns the team adopts.
About You
We care about how good you are and how far you can go, and we calibrate to the experience you bring. This seat is built for exceptional people - whether you are just out of a top program or already have a few years of serious building behind you.
An excellent engineer who ships. You write excellent code and have built real things, full-stack across a Python backend and a React frontend - or you are clearly able to get there fast.
Hungry and driven. You want a hard problem to own, not a comfortable seat, and you have the ceiling to grow into far more.
Rigorous with non-deterministic systems. You spec and eval before shipping, trust evidence over vibes, and own what goes out - including AI-assisted code - following problems into production.
AI-native and curious. You understand how agent frameworks, tools, and evals actually work under the hood, and you build with AI coding tools every day.
Calm in fast-moving ambiguity. You stay effective on a stack where this quarter's best practice changes next quarter, turning uncertainty into a workable plan.
Nice to have: real AI/agent product experience (MCP, agent frameworks, evals); durable workflow engines (e.g. Temporal); streaming UIs; observability (OpenTelemetry); spec-driven development; multi-tenant SaaS, or aerospace/defense/discrete-manufacturing context.
Why Pelico
If You Want To Build Something Hard From The Ground Up, With Real Ownership From Day One, This Is The Seat. What Comes With It
A founding team and a real mandate. You help build Condor from its early days, with genuine ownership of what you ship and room to grow fast.
The highest-stakes work you could take on. You build for some of the largest manufacturers, at the scale of their global operations, on a moat competitors cannot copy: we own both the factory simulation and the scoreboard that says whether an agent actually helped.
A small, elite, AI-native team. Be challenged by strong peers, learn quickly, and ship fast.
Competitive salary benchmarked to your market, plus health, dental, and vision coverage and a learning budget.

In this role, you will contribute to the architecture, design, development, verification, and release of FPGA-based solutions supporting next-generation power management products. Working alongside global, cross-functional teams, you will play a key role in bringing new products to market, including advanced silicon carbide (SiC)-based three-phase power conversion systems that deliver reliable power for mission-critical applications such as data centers.
The expected annual salary range for this role is $80000 - $118000 a year.
Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

Work as part of an engineering team to architect, develop, verify, test, and release FPGA-based designs in support of new product development. Review product requirements and collaborate with systems, firmware, controls, power electronics, and hardware engineers to translate system-level specifications into FPGA architecture and detailed design requirements.

Design, develop, review, and maintain synthesizable RTL using Verilog, SystemVerilog, and/or VHDL.

Develop testbenches and perform RTL simulation and functional verification to ensure designs meet functional and system requirements.

Analyze and resolve FPGA implementation challenges related to timing, resource utilization, clock distribution, reset architecture, and clock-domain crossing.
Design and integrate communication interfaces between FPGAs, microcontrollers, DSPs, ADCs, DACs, and other system components using interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet, and parallel interfaces, as applicable.

Professional experience developing synthesizable RTL using VHDL, Verilog, and/or SystemVerilog.
Experience with FPGA design workflows including RTL development, simulation, synthesis, implementation, timing analysis, and hardware validation.
Design experience with power electronic, industrial control, energy conversion, or other real-time embedded products.
Experience implementing digital control algorithms, PWM generation, modulation techniques and high-speed deterministic control functions in FPGA.
Experience with FPGA development toolchains such as Intel Quartus, and ModelSim/Questa.
Experience integrating FPGA designs with microcontrollers, DSPs, ADCs, DACs, and mixed-signal embedded systems.
Experience implementing communication interfaces such as SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, Ethernet, and high-speed serial or parallel interfaces.
Experience with embedded firmware development and programming in C/C++.
Experience using hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) simulation for system integration and validation.
Skills
Strong knowledge of digital logic design, synchronous design principles, finite-state machines, pipelining, clocking, reset architectures, and FPGA resource optimization.
Understanding of three-phase electrical power systems and power conversion concepts is preferred.
Ability to read and understand electrical schematics, component datasheets, interface specifications, and timing diagrams.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively in cross-functional and geographically distributed engineering teams.
Self-motivated, proactive, detail-oriented, and capable of independently driving technical activities to meet project schedules.
Ability to work in a laboratory environment around high-voltage equipment where strict adherence to safety practices is critical.

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.
At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.
Role Overview
As a Software Engineer on the Security Engineering team at Harvey, you'll build and operate foundational security services for both our customer-facing product and the internal systems our workforce depends on: encryption and key management, public key infrastructure (PKI), secrets management, and shared controls for identity, secure software delivery, and agent execution. You'll turn security needs into production systems and own the reliability and security of what you build, working closely with engineers and partner teams along the way. Attackers increasingly operate at agent speed, so we’re building defenses that can keep pace.
Security at Harvey is an engineering discipline, not a gatekeeper function. We build platforms and libraries that make it hard for engineers to get security wrong, and we measure ourselves on adoption and outcomes rather than tickets filed. Our program is informed by risk: we invest where the actual exposure to our most sensitive data and resources is greatest, rather than where a framework tells us to.
What You'll Do
Build and operate services for encryption, key management, and secure storage across product and infrastructure systems, working closely with partner teams
Implement and improve PKI and secrets management workflows, including certificate renewal, secure credential delivery, rotation, and revocation
Build identity controls, sandboxes, and safety harnesses that let services and AI agents operate with least privilege, constrained actions, clear auditability, and effective monitoring
Create secure-by-default libraries and self-service tooling that make encryption, secrets handling, and other shared security controls easy to adopt
Build code, dependency, and secret scanning integrations, CI/CD controls, and agentic workflows that automate security triage, remediation, and evidence collection
Take security systems from design through production, accounting for trust boundaries, attacker paths, and operational failure modes while owning their reliability and security
Share an on-call rotation for Harvey’s mission-critical security services, contribute to incident response, and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and clear documentation
What You Have
2+ years of software engineering experience, including experience shipping and operating production services
Experience building or contributing to security infrastructure in one or more areas such as encryption and key management, PKI, secrets management, secure software delivery, or identity and access
Strong programming, debugging, testing, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work across unfamiliar systems and domains
Experience with cloud infrastructure such as Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or Amazon Web Services and familiarity with modern distributed-system patterns
A track record of translating security requirements into maintainable, automated systems
Experience using agentic coding tools and creating workflows that automate repetitive security work, with the judgment to review their output critically and measure whether they improve security outcomes
Clear communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to explain technical risks, decisions, and tradeoffs to engineering partners
Working knowledge of common vulnerability classes and the ability to reason about how a system fails under an attacker, not just under load
Nice to Have
Experience building security infrastructure at a fast-growing company
Familiarity with applied cryptography, such as using established cryptographic libraries, encryption APIs, or cloud key management services (KMS)
Experience with TLS/mTLS, certificate lifecycle automation, or secrets management platforms
Experience securing agentic or AI-powered systems, especially systems that act on behalf of users against sensitive data
Experience working in a highly regulated enterprise environment

Life @ Pave

control, build confidence, and earn credibility

Embedded systems
FPGA and firmware development
CPU/GPU architectures
RF and antenna systems
Digital signal processing solutions
Fully integrated hardware/software systems
